findings.title: Swapped storage and legacy duration metrics in Create, Update, and DeleteCollection
findings.body:
Several metric recording calls in `DualWriterMode3` record against the wrong storage backend metric:
- Line 45 (`Create`): When `d.Storage.Create` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.
- Line 129 (`Update`): When `d.Storage.Update` fails, `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.
- Line 166 (`DeleteCollection`): Inside the async legacy goroutine, `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` is called for `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, ...)`.

This skews latency and error metrics by attributing unified storage errors to legacy storage and legacy collection-delete latencies/errors to unified storage.

findings.title: Async legacy writes derive from the request context and will be canceled when the handler returns
findings.body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutines derive their timeout context directly from the incoming request context via `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)`. Because the outer method returns immediately after spawning the goroutine, the HTTP server finishes the request and cancels `ctx`, which immediately cancels the child context in the background goroutine and causes the asynchronous `d.Legacy` writes to fail with `context.Canceled`. The background context should detach from parent cancellation first (e.g., `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, ...)`).

findings.title: Data race on input object and UpdatedObjectInfo between synchronous response and async legacy write
findings.body:
In `Create` (line 55) and `Update` (line 139), the input `obj` and `objInfo` are passed directly into the background goroutine calling `d.Legacy.Create` and `d.Legacy.Update` while the main goroutine returns `created`/`res` to the apiserver handler for serialization:
- In `Create`, `d.Storage.Create` and `d.Legacy.Create` (via strategy `PrepareForCreate`/validation) can mutate `obj` in place concurrently with the caller serializing `created`.
- In `Update`, `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` (such as `rest.DefaultUpdatedObjectInfo`) holds a single decoded `runtime.Object` that is mutated in place when `UpdatedObject` is called. Calling `d.Legacy.Update` concurrently with the same `objInfo` re-runs `UpdatedObject` and mutates the same object while the HTTP response is being serialized.

A deep copy of the object created/updated by `d.Storage` should be passed to the background goroutine instead.

findings.title: Delete attaches unenriched logger to context instead of `log`
findings.body: In `Delete`, line 96 constructs `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 calls `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. Any downstream code retrieving the logger from `ctx` will miss the `name`, `kind`, and `method` fields.

findings.title: Delete passes object `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the `kind` metric label
findings.body: On line 106 in `Delete`, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the individual object's `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the `kind` label parameter. In addition to recording an incorrect `kind` label on successful deletes, `name` is an unbounded per-resource identifier and will cause high-cardinality metric explosion in Prometheus.

findings.title: Mode 3 unit tests share a single mock between stores and do not synchronize with async legacy calls
findings.body:
In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go`, `ls` and `us` are initialized with the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` instance, and the tests do not synchronize with the background goroutines spawned by `Create`, `Delete`, `DeleteCollection`, and `Update`:
- Because `ls` and `us` share `m`, expectations set on `m` match calls to either store. For example, in `TestMode3_Create` (line 40, "error when creating object in the unified store fails"), the test configures `setupLegacyFn` instead of `setupStorageFn` and only passes because both stores use `m`.
- None of the write tests wait for the background `d.Legacy` goroutine to complete or assert that `d.Legacy` was invoked, causing the background goroutine to race with test completion while recording metrics on the shared package-level Prometheus registry `p`.
